title: Hom from a finitely presented module on a qcqs space commutes with directed colimits
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the small etale site and quasi-coherence of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume $|X|$ is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover, with topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]) and that its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. A module is of finite presentation if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O^{m}\to\mathcal O^{n}$ with $m,n$ finite. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed preorder, let $(\mathcal M_i)$ be a diagram of module sheaves, and let $(\mathcal M,(c_i))$ be its colimit in module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For a module $\mathcal G$ of finite presentation, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M_i)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M)$ is bijective. Explicitly every map $\mathcal G\to\mathcal M$ factors as $c_i g$ at some stage, and if $c_i g=c_j h$, there is $k\ge i,j$ with the two induced maps to $\mathcal M_k$ equal. The modules $\mathcal M_i$ need not be quasi-coherent.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $\mathcal H_i=\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M_i)$, with transitions given by postcomposition. These are module sheaves, and their global sections are $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M_i)$ by the sheaf-Hom definition. Check the technical site hypotheses of the internal-Hom continuity theorem as follows. The universe convention makes $\mathcal C$ and each iterated slice small in the module universe. Apply sieve-module sheafification with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ on each such site: abelian presheaves are exactly $\mathbf Z$-module presheaves by the unique repeated-addition action, so its reflector gives abelian sheafification. The locally-bijective characterization of abelian sheafification applies to every such site. Finally, forgetting commutativity of a ring sheaf preserves the sheaf condition: the underlying sections, restrictions and unique gluings are identical. Thus all the sheafification, local-bijection and ring-forgetting hypotheses in the cited continuity theorem hold; no finiteness property of $\mathcal M_i$ is involved.

source.place: Tag 0GMZ (lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit), setup; internal Hom: Tag 03EM (lemma-internal-hom). General-site sheafification hypotheses are supplied by the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: The given finite-presentation hypothesis says precisely that $\mathcal G$ locally admits a finite presentation on $\mathcal C$. Apply the site finite-presentation internal-Hom continuity theorem to $\mathcal G$ and the small filtered diagram $i\mapsto\mathcal M_i$. A nonempty directed preorder is filtered: finitely many objects have a common upper bound by induction, and parallel arrows are equal. The resulting isomorphism is the canonical map $$a:\varinjlim_i\mathcal H_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M),$$ whose composite with the $i$th coprojection sends a local map $g$ to $c_i\circ g$.

source.place: Tag 0GMZ (lemma-hom-finite-presentation-colimit), conclusion; Tag 0GN0 (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-compact-colimit), proof, H = colim H_lambda.

proof.text: Write $L=\varinjlim_i\mathcal H_i$ in module sheaves. The module forgetful theorem identifies its underlying abelian sheaf with the colimit of the underlying abelian sheaves of $\mathcal H_i$, with the same coprojections. Apply algebraic-space cohomology continuity in degree $q=0$ to this abelian diagram. Its hypotheses are exactly the quasi-compactness and absolute quasi-separatedness assumed for $X$. Consequently $$\varinjlim_i\Gamma(X,\mathcal H_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma(X,L).$$ Here $H^0=\Gamma$ canonically: global sections are additive and left exact (a compatible family of sections in a kernel is exactly a compatible family mapping to zero); the cited degree-zero injective-resolution theorem therefore identifies their zeroth derived functor with global sections. This does not require $X$ to be a scheme or a final object of its scheme etale site.

source.place: Tag 073E (lemma-colimits), q=0; sites-cohomology.tex, section-cohomology-sheaves, equation-cohomology; sites-modules.tex Tag 03DB (lemma-limits-colimits).

proof.text: Compose the isomorphism of step 3 with $\Gamma(a)$ from step 2 and use the global-section formula for sheaf Hom. This gives $$\varinjlim_i\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal G,\mathcal M).$$ On the $i$th coprojection it sends $g$ to $c_i\circ g$, so it is the canonical map in the statement, not an unspecified bijection. Forgetting abelian groups preserves filtered colimits, and the elementwise set-colimit theorem says every element has a stage representative and equality is witnessed at a common later stage. Applying it to this map proves both explicit assertions, with $k\ge i,j$ since the arrows of $I$ are its order relations.
